 News Flash
 Tropical Update: Severe Weather Expected Through Sunday, Nov. 22
 Emergency Management
 Posted on November 19, 2026 
 PUBLIC NOTICE
 The National Weather Service Forecast Office in Wilmington (NWS-Wilmington) is currently predicting potential severe weather impacts starting Friday, Nov. 20 through Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026, that would affect Brunswick County and surrounding counties.
 Confidence is slowly increasing regarding the potential for a coastal storm with a medium chance (60%) of it becoming subtropical or tropical this weekend. Any potential storm impacts will be similar regardless of the storm type (tropical, subtropical, etc.). Potential impacts include heavy rainfall, gusty winds, rough surf, minor coastal flooding, and beach erosion.  The greatest impacts are expected over the coastal waters, especially Saturday through Sunday. Prepare for dangerous maritime operations and navigation. 
 This is an evolving situation, and weather forecasts are subject to change. Remain alert for updates from the NWS-Wilmington at weather.gov/ilm and find the latest weather briefing at weather.gov/ilm/briefing .
 Brunswick County will share additional updates as necessary.
 What You Should Do Now / Safety Reminders
 Make a plan. Create and practice a Family Emergency Communication Plan that includes all members of your household and pets. Discuss your household evacuation plan for every member of the household and pets . Review your insurance policies (including flood insurance ) to ensure your property is covered for any flooding or natural disasters that could occur.
 Build a kit.  An emergency kit is vital for your survival in situations where help might not be easily accessible due to power outages and road damage. When preparing an emergency kit, it is recommended to prepare three to seven days’ worth of medicine, water , and non-perishable food for each person and pet in your home. Make copies of your important documents and store them physically and digitally in secure locations.
 Stay informed.  Ensure you have multiple ways you will receive credible and accurate information before, during, and after a tropical event. To get updates from Brunswick County, sign up for the ReadyBrunswick Emergency Notification System , subscribe to our Sunshine List and Emergency Updates email lists , and follow Brunswick County on social media .
 Stay alert about road closures. Prepare for potential hazardous travel, including road closures. In the event roads flood, always remember— Turn Around, Don’t Drown! Never drive, walk, or swim through flooded roadways or past barricades on roads. For the latest information on road closures, download or check the Brunswick County Sheriff’s Office Mobile App and DriveNC.gov .
 Prepare your property.  Take time to learn how to prepare your home/property before, during, and after a storm . Secure any loose items and furniture on your property ahead of the storm. Practice home safety skills to protect your family and property.
 Know the terms. Review the terms and categories used by weather professionals and public safety officials for tropical cyclones. A Watch means BE PREPARED, a severe weather event is possible in or near the watch area. A Warning means TAKE ACTION, as a severe weather event is happening or is about to happen.
 Report power outages and downed electrical lines.  If you experience a power outage or see downed electrical lines, report it to your electric provider. Remember that electric crews will have to wait for safe conditions to begin restoring power. Duke Energy Progress:  Report at duke-energy.com/outages , text OUT to 57801 , call 800.419.6356 , or use the Duke Energy App .
 Brunswick Electric Membership Corporation (BEMC):  Report at bemc.org/report-power-outage , text OUTAGE to 800.682.5309 , call 800.682.5309 , or use the BEMC SmartHub App .
 For more severe weather preparedness tips from Brunswick County, visit BrunswickCountyNC.gov/hurricanes .
 View updates from the National Hurricane Center, a real-time emergency weather map, and additional online resources at nhc.noaa.gov .
